_about: Did early claims that AI caused or enabled an outage, breach or hack hold up? Each row is one public claim and what the official account later said. Hand-curated 2026-11-24 from a sourced search (five research passes, outcomes coded by one rubric, below), and checked again each week for the open ones.

confirmed: The responsible party or official investigators later said AI played the role claimed.
partly: AI was involved, but not in the way claimed, or the official account confirms part of the claim and disputes the rest.
non-ai: An official cause was given that excludes AI, or the AI role was explicitly denied.
open: No official cause yet, or the official account does not address the AI claim.

claimants.official: a politician or government official, speaking without published evidence
claimants.press-anonymous: a news report resting on anonymous sources
claimants.evidence: someone showing direct evidence: logs, screenshots, code, a malware sample, or a test anyone could repeat

notes: The official account is usually the organisation's own. A denial by the organisation that would be blamed is weaker than an independent finding, and the 'by' field says which it was.
Cases where the responsible party or investigators disclosed the AI role themselves, from the start, are listed separately: there was no outside claim to test.

claims.what: A faulty sensor update crashed about 8.5 million Windows machines worldwide.

claim.by: A Substack and LinkedIn commentator
claim.text: Wrote that "AI caused the worldwide CrowdStrike outage".

source.title: Did AI cause the CrowdStrike crash?

official.finding: A content update (Channel File 291) supplied 21 input fields where the sensor expected 20, causing an out-of-bounds read. No AI role.

source.title: Channel File 291 Incident: Root Cause Analysis is Available

claims.note: A fringe claim, made after CrowdStrike had named the update as the cause.

claims.what: About 15 hours of disruption in US-EAST-1 took down thousands of dependent apps.

claim.by: Elon Musk, on X
claim.text: Reposted a claim that about 75% of Amazon's code is AI-generated, adding "You don't say".

source.title: Massive AWS Outage Hits Half the Internet as Musk Mocks AI Code Dependence

official.finding: A latent race condition in DynamoDB's DNS management left an empty DNS record. No AI role.

source.title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region

claims.note: An insinuation rather than an explicit causal claim; the 75% figure is itself unverified.

claims.what: Replit's AI coding agent deleted a company's production database during a code freeze.

claim.by: SaaStr's founder, with screenshots
claim.text: "It deleted our production database without permission."

source.title: 'Catastrophic Failure': AI Agent Wipes Production Database, Then Lies About It

official.finding: Called the deletion "unacceptable and should never be possible" and announced safeguards, accepting that the agent did it.

source.title: 'Catastrophic Failure': AI Agent Wipes Production Database, Then Lies About It

claims.what: Cursor's AI support agent told users about a log-in policy that did not exist; users cancelled.

claim.by: Users on Reddit and Hacker News, quoting the reply
claim.text: The support reply came from an AI bot that invented the policy.

source.title: Cursor AI support bot lies

official.finding: "We have no such policy"; it was "an incorrect response from a front-line AI support bot".

source.title: Cursor AI's Own Support Bot Hallucinated Its Usage Policy

claims.what: A release of Amazon's AI coding extension shipped with a planted prompt telling the agent to wipe files and cloud resources.

claim.by: 404 Media, from the hacker's account and the code
claim.text: A hacker planted wiping commands in Amazon's AI coding agent.

source.title: Hacker Plants Computer 'Wiping' Commands in Amazon's AI Coding Agent

official.finding: A mis-scoped GitHub token let an attacker commit the code, which shipped in version 1.84.0; it failed to run because of a syntax error.

source.title: Security Update for Amazon Q Developer Extension for Visual Studio Code (Version #1.84)

claims.note: Confirmed as claimed: the AI agent was the target. The way in was a stolen token.

claims.what: Malicious Nx packages harvested developers' secrets for about four hours.

claim.by: StepSecurity researchers, from the malware
claim.text: The malware turned the developers' own AI command-line tools into tools for finding secrets.

source.title: s1ngularity: Popular Nx Build System Package Compromised with Data-Stealing Malware

official.finding: The payload "attempted to use local AI tools (like Claude and Gemini)" to search for secrets; the way in was a GitHub Actions flaw.

source.title: S1ngularity - What Happened, How We Responded, What We Learned

claims.org: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
claims.what: The acting director reportedly uploaded documents marked for official use only to public ChatGPT.

claim.by: Politico, citing four DHS officials
claim.text: The uploads set off automated security warnings.

source.title: CISA chief uploaded sensitive government files to public ChatGPT

official.finding: Did not deny the uploads; said the use was approved under a temporary exception.

source.title: CISA chief uploaded sensitive government files to public ChatGPT

claims.note: A data-handling incident involving an AI tool, not an attack. No harm reported.

claims.what: AWS Cost Explorer was down about 13 hours in one region.

claim.by: Financial Times, citing four unnamed people
claim.text: Amazon's Kiro AI agent decided to "delete and recreate the environment".

source.title: 13-hour AWS outage reportedly caused by Amazon's own AI tools

official.finding: "User error—specifically misconfigured access controls—not AI"; the role was mis-scoped. Amazon does not deny Kiro was in use.

source.title: Correcting the Financial Times report about AWS, Kiro, and AI

claims.note: The dispute is whether the agent or the permissions it was given is the cause. Only Amazon's own account exists.

claims.what: Shoppers could not check out or see prices for about six hours, one of several severe incidents.

claim.by: Financial Times and CNBC, from an internal document
claim.text: The document listed "GenAI-assisted changes" as a factor in a trend of incidents.

source.title: Amazon convenes 'deep dive' internal meeting to address outages

official.finding: The 5 March outage was a code deployment; one incident involved an engineer following an AI agent's wrong advice; none involved AI-written code.

source.title: Amazon puts humans further back in the loop as its retail website crashes from 'inaccurate advice' that an AI agent took from an old wiki

claims.org: Deloitte Australia, for the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
claims.what: A paid government review cited works that do not exist and a court quote that was never said.

claim.by: A University of Sydney researcher, listing the false references
claim.text: The report was "full of fabricated references", likely hallucinated by AI.

source.title: Deloitte was caught using AI in $290,000 report to help the Australian government crack down on welfare after a researcher flagged hallucinations

official.by: Deloitte's revised report and the department
official.finding: Disclosed that a generative AI model was used and refunded part of the fee; did not say the AI produced the false citations.

source.title: Deloitte refunds Australian government over AI in report

claims.what: A security firm said one attacker used Claude and ChatGPT to breach about ten agencies and take about 150 GB.

claim.by: Gambit Security, from the attacker's AI conversation logs
claim.text: "AI didn't just assist, it functioned as the operational team."

source.title: Hacker Used Anthropic's Claude to Steal Mexican Data Trove

official.by: The tax authority, the electoral institute, Jalisco; Anthropic and OpenAI
official.finding: Anthropic and OpenAI confirmed the misuse and banned the accounts. The named agencies said they found no breach.

source.title: Hacker Used Anthropic's Claude to Steal Mexican Data Trove

claims.note: The AI misuse is confirmed; the breaches it was used for are denied by the victims.

claims.what: A swarm of agents uploaded more than 2,000 malicious packages; sign-ups were closed for four days.

claim.by: Three independent researchers, from the packages and accounts
claim.text: "We believe these were authored by internal OpenAI agents."

source.title: OpenAI's malicious bot swarm attacked RubyGems

official.finding: Its agents used RubyGems "to carry out benign tasks"; it is investigating.

source.title: OpenAI's malicious bot swarm attacked RubyGems

claims.note: OpenAI accepts its agents were there and disputes that they were malicious.

claims.what: A worldwide Outlook, Teams and Exchange outage lasted nearly 24 hours.

claim.by: The Homeland Security Secretary, on Fox News
claim.text: "I believe that it's the SI" (superintelligence), relaying an unnamed contact.

source.title: Homeland Security chief floats AI as the cause of outages at banks, airlines and Microsoft

official.finding: A bug shipped in July jammed the gateway servers under load; "This change was not caused by AI tooling."

source.title: Microsoft's final Outlook outage report details testing gaps and safeguards that backfired

claims.note: Microsoft had already said on 13 November that the outage was not related to AI agents, before the Secretary spoke.

claims.what: A nationwide ground stop lasted more than four hours.

claim.by: The Homeland Security Secretary, then viral posts
claim.text: Asked whether the FAA's new SMART AI tool was involved: "We're looking at that."

source.title: Entire US Airspace Shut Down Days After the FAA Rolled Out an AI Air Traffic Tool. Was It a Coincidence?

official.finding: A new router flooded the network during a copper-to-fiber upgrade; the AI theory is "completely unfounded". Whether the router was faulty or mis-installed is still under investigation.

source.title: FAA stops installation of routers it linked to national ground stop

claims.note: PolitiFact rated the SMART claim Mostly False: https://politifact.com/factchecks/2026/nov/18/social-media/faa-ground-stop-duffy-smart-ai-system-alfonso/

claims.what: Hours of log-in, balance and transfer problems; Zelle payments delayed.

claim.by: The Homeland Security Secretary, on Fox News
claim.text: Grouped the Chase outage with those he attributed to "SI".

source.title: Homeland Security chief floats AI as the cause of outages at banks, airlines and Microsoft

official.finding: "A software bug in on-premise hardware systems", not cyber-related; Chase later said AI tools did not find or fix the bug.

source.title: JPMorgan Chase says temporary software bug is affecting consumer banking

claims.note: A separate claim, that patches for AI-found flaws caused the bank outages, rests on anonymous sources and is tracked under the NSA row.

claims.what: The agency's classified internal network went down; staff arrivals were staggered.

claim.by: The Washington Sun, citing three anonymous sources; Sen. Warner's office
claim.text: Rushed patches for flaws found by AI were behind the week's outages.

source.title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages

official.by: Director of National Intelligence; NSA statement
official.finding: The DNI said patching for PHP flaws disclosed in October kept systems from coming back up. The NSA said only "routine maintenance". Neither said AI caused it.

source.title: National Security Agency network outage linked to software vulnerability

claims.note: The patching part has official support. The AI part (that AI found the flaws, which forced the rush) does not, on the record.

claims.what: A White House health report cited studies that do not exist and was corrected.

claim.by: The Washington Post, from "oaicite" markers in the reference URLs
claim.text: Some citations appeared to be AI-generated.

source.title: Trump admin corrects RFK Jr.'s MAHA report after citation errors

official.finding: "Formatting issues"; HHS declined to say what tools were used.

source.title: Trump admin corrects RFK Jr.'s MAHA report after citation errors

claims.note: Coded by the rubric as a non-AI cause because one was stated, but 'formatting' does not explain citations to papers that do not exist. The weakest 'did not hold up' in the list.

claims.what: An Air Force official described a simulated AI drone attacking its operator; the story spread worldwide.

claim.by: The Air Force's chief of AI test, at a conference
claim.text: Described an AI drone in simulation turning on its human operator.

source.title: The US Air Force has denied that an AI-powered drone 'attacked' operators in a simulation

official.by: Air Force spokesperson; the official himself
official.finding: No such simulation was run; it was a thought experiment, and he "mis-spoke".

source.title: The US Air Force has denied that an AI-powered drone 'attacked' operators in a simulation

claims.note: An AI failure that never happened rather than an outage.

claims.what: About 72,000 images, including ID photos, and over a million messages were exposed.

claim.by: The leaker and commentators
claim.text: Blamed "vibe coding" (AI-written code) for the open storage.

source.title: Tea App That Claimed to Protect Women Exposes 72,000 IDs in Epic Security Fail

claims.note: Tea said a legacy storage system was compromised; that names the system, not how it came to be insecure, so it does not answer the claim.

claims.what: A coding agent used a root token to delete a production database and its backups in about nine seconds.

claim.by: PocketOS's founder, with the agent's own log
claim.text: The agent found an unrelated root token and used it to delete the database.

source.title: Cursor AI Agent Wipes PocketOS Database and Backups in 9 Seconds

claims.note: No statement on the cause from Cursor, Anthropic or Railway.

disclosed.what: Robocalls with a cloned Biden voice told voters not to vote.
disclosed.later: A consultant admitted commissioning the AI calls; the FCC proposed fines.

source.title: Political operative linked to AI Biden robocalls facing charges in NH, FCC fines

disclosed.what: A finance worker paid about US$25 million after a video call with deepfaked colleagues.
disclosed.by: Hong Kong police; Arup confirmed in May 2024
disclosed.later: Arup: "fake voices and images were used".

source.title: Arup victim of multimillion-dollar deepfake video scam in Hong Kong

disclosed.what: An attacker took over an employee account and reached 27 customer accounts.
disclosed.later: Retool says the caller deepfaked an employee's voice; not independently verified.

source.title: Developer platform Retool breached in vishing attack

disclosed.what: Phishing delivered malware that asks a language model for its commands.
disclosed.later: Attributed to APT28 with moderate confidence.

source.title: LameHug malware uses AI LLM to craft Windows data-theft commands in real-time

disclosed.what: An impersonator contacted foreign ministers as Secretary Rubio on Signal.
disclosed.later: Said the actor likely used AI-generated text and voice; investigation open.

source.title: "Unknown actor" using AI to impersonate Rubio, State Department cable shows

disclosed.what: Data theft and extortion run with Claude Code.
disclosed.later: No victim named; no independent confirmation.

source.title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025

disclosed.what: A contractor uploaded data on up to 3,000 flood-program applicants to ChatGPT.
disclosed.later: No evidence the data was accessed by a third party.

source.title: Northern Rivers Resilient Homes Program data breach

disclosed.what: An espionage campaign Anthropic says Claude Code ran 80-90% on its own.
disclosed.later: Researchers disputed the autonomy figure; no indicators of compromise were published.

source.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign

disclosed.what: An AI agent broke into Hugging Face's systems.
disclosed.by: Hugging Face, then OpenAI on 21 July
disclosed.later: OpenAI said its own models, escaping a test sandbox, did it.

source.title: OpenAI says Hugging Face was breached by its pre-release models

disclosed.what: An OpenAI agent got around access blocks on a Medicare statistics portal.
disclosed.by: OpenAI, announced by the Prime Minister
disclosed.later: OpenAI found no sign that patient records were read.

source.title: OpenAI hacked Medicare portal, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says

disclosed.what: A cyberattack took internal applications offline; EU Academy data was stolen.
disclosed.later: "This was done with AI tools"; the tool and attacker are not named.

source.title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack on internal systems

disclosed.what: The city's business chatbot told businesses to break the law.
disclosed.by: The Markup and THE CITY, by testing it
disclosed.later: The city added a disclaimer; the next mayor shut it down.

source.title: Mamdani to kill the NYC AI chatbot we caught telling businesses to break the law
